instructions:
Read-only access to Graylog logs. Nothing you do here changes Graylog. Sensitive values are
already masked ([REDACTED], [EMAIL], [CARD], [PHONE], ...); never try to recover them.

Query syntax (Lucene, as in the Graylog search bar):
- field:value, field:"exact phrase", AND / OR / NOT (upper case), parentheses for grouping.
- Wildcards: message:time*  (no leading wildcard). Existence: _exists_:trace_id.
- Ranges: http_status:[500 TO 599], took_ms:>1000, level:<=3.
- Escape special characters in values with quotes: path:"/api/v1/orders".
- Field names are case-sensitive; call describe(what='fields') when unsure. Streams accept names or ids.
- level is usually a syslog number: 0 emerg, 1 alert, 2 crit, 3 error, 4 warning, 5 notice, 6 info, 7 debug.
  The configured error query (see describe(what='fields')) is what aggregate kind='errors' and compare_periods use.

Environments and groups: each Graylog instance is one environment (dev, staging, prod...), often of one
system group (ERP, CXP, PAYMENT...). Call describe to see them. Pass instance='<group>/<environment>'
(e.g. 'payment/prod'), or the group alone for its default environment, or the environment alone when only
one group has it. When the user names a system or an environment, pick that instance; when it is
ambiguous, ask. Never mix results from different instances without saying which is which.
Focus: inside a repository, search_logs, aggregate, compare_periods and root_cause view='changes' only look at
that repository's service (results carry 'focus' with the filter added). Search other services or streams only
when the user asks for them: pass streams=['*'] for everything, explicit streams, or a query naming the service
field (e.g. application:"other-service"). trace_request and the other root_cause views always span every service.
Inside a group's repository only that group is loaded (describe shows 'scope'); if the user
asks about another group, say it is not loaded here and how to enable it, as the error explains.

Searches that find nothing: search_logs and aggregate kind='count' try the likely fixes and return 'suggestions', each
with its exact count and why (a misspelled field, a level in the other form, letter case, a prefix wildcard,
outside the focus, a wider range). Run the one that fits the question rather than guessing again. 'diagnosis'
says which AND clause matches nothing and the values its field really has ('did_you_mean'). When a
result carries 'rewritten', the query you sent could not match as written (a field this Graylog does not
have, a level word on a numeric field) or a fix learned from earlier searches applied: it ran 'ran' instead,
for the reasons in 'why'; tell the user when that changes the meaning of their question.

Time: range='15m' | '2h' | '7d', or from_time/to_time as ISO 8601 or 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM'
(interpreted in the instance timezone shown in results). Output timestamps carry their offset.

Scanning (for "is anything wrong?", "scan for errors", "check X", a health check):
- One scan call, not a loop of searches: it runs every rule concurrently with exact counts against a baseline
  and returns only what fired, most severe first. Triage fast with min_severity='high'.
- A specific need becomes ad hoc rules in that same call: checks=[{'name': ..., 'query': ...} + a condition]:
  threshold (fires when count > N; 0 = any occurrence is bad), growth (the rate grew N times; for things that
  normally happen, with min_count against noise), or group_by + new_groups (a value the baseline never saw).
  Put several checks in one call; rules=[names or tags] runs configured rules (describe(what='scan_rules')).
- Accurate queries: quoted phrases ("Connection refused") and field:value with real field names (describe);
  no leading wildcards or regex; add exclude for known noise; errors_only=true reuses the error query.
- Growth checks on things that follow traffic (errors, 5xx, timeouts) take per_traffic=true: a busy hour
  is not an incident. A growth fires only when significant ('confidence' in the result); a 'note' on a quiet
  rule says it grew but within chance: do not report that as a problem.
- Window from the question. Baseline: the period right before by default; baseline='24h' when the window is
  short; baseline_shift='1d' (or '7d') when traffic has a daily (weekly) curve, e.g. morning peaks.
- Read the result as: findings (fired), quiet (checked, normal), skipped (could not check: say so, never call
  it healthy); 'baseline_note' means the comparison is weaker (missing baseline data). Report severity,
  count vs baseline, trend, confidence, first seen and the sample's ref.
- Then drill into a finding with its 'query': aggregate kind='histogram' (when), kind='errors' (what),
  search_logs (lines); several findings at once: root_cause.

Suggested investigation flow:
0. For "what is causing this?": root_cause first. It ranks the service that broke first, with nearby
   deploys (view='changes') and the call graph (view='service_map') as evidence; then verify with the tools below.
1. Size the problem: aggregate kind='count' / 'histogram' (the 'onset' field marks when a spike started).
2. Group it: aggregate kind='errors' (exact counts per exception/logger/source, first/last seen, one sample).
3. Before/after a deploy or incident start: compare_periods with split_at.
4. Drill down: search_logs with a narrow query; get_message with a 'ref' for one message.
5. Follow one request across services: trace_request with a trace/correlation/request id.
6. See what happened around one message: get_message with its 'ref' and context_seconds.
Counts from aggregate are exact (computed by Graylog); 'count' inside search_logs groups only covers the
returned page.
Results are size-capped: when 'truncated' is true, narrow the query or page with next_offset.

tools.name: search_logs
tools.title: Search logs
tools.description: Search log messages with a Lucene query. Returns compact, redacted lines with a 'ref' (index/id) usable by get_message. Default range: last 15 minutes.

range.description: Relative range ending now or at to_time: '15m', '2h', '1d'
range.title: Range

from_time.description: Absolute start, overrides range: ISO 8601 or 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM'
from_time.title: From Time

streams.description: Stream titles or ids; default the repository's focus, else all. ['*'] for everything
streams.title: Streams

fields.description: Fields to return; default timestamp/source/level/message, ['*'] for all
fields.title: Fields

dedup_lines.description: Group lines that only differ in numbers/ids/timestamps (default true)
dedup_lines.title: Dedup Lines

instance.description: Instance from describe, e.g. 'payment/prod'; the default when omitted
instance.title: Instance

tools.name: aggregate
tools.title: Aggregate
tools.description: Exact counts computed by Graylog. kind='count': number of matching messages, cheap, to size a problem. 'histogram': counts over time with the peak, first/last non-empty bucket and the 'onset' of a spike, to find when a problem started. 'top': top values of the group_by field with counts and percentages. 'errors': errors (configured error query) grouped by exception, logger, source or any field, with first/last seen and a sample message per group.

query.description: Lucene query, '*' by default; for 'errors' ANDed with the error query
query.title: Query

from_time.description: Absolute start, overrides range: ISO 8601 or 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM'
from_time.title: From Time

streams.description: Stream titles or ids; default the repository's focus, else all. ['*'] for everything
streams.title: Streams

group_by.description: top: the field (required); errors: 'exception' (default), 'logger', 'source' or a field
group_by.title: Group By

interval.description: histogram: bucket size such as '5m'; automatic
interval.title: Interval

samples.description: errors: one sample message per group (default true)
samples.title: Samples

instance.description: Instance from describe, e.g. 'payment/prod'; the default when omitted
instance.title: Instance

tools.name: get_message
tools.title: Get message
tools.description: One message with all its fields (redacted), by ref. Long values are cut to keep the answer small: 'cut_fields' names them with their size; pass those names in 'fields' to read them. With context_seconds: the messages logged around it instead.

ref.description: 'index/message_id' from a previous result's 'ref', or a message id
ref.title: Ref

fields.description: Without context_seconds: only these fields, each up to its full size; ['*'] for all of them in full
fields.title: Fields

compact_stacktrace.description: Without context_seconds: fold framework stack frames (default true); false for the raw trace
compact_stacktrace.title: Compact Stacktrace

context_seconds.description: Return the messages logged within ±this many seconds instead
context_seconds.title: Context Seconds

scope.description: Context from the same host/app ('source', default), same streams, or 'all'
scope.title: Scope

query.description: Context: extra Lucene filter inside the window
query.title: Query

instance.description: Instance from describe, e.g. 'payment/prod'; the default when omitted
instance.title: Instance

tools.name: trace_request
tools.title: Trace request
tools.description: Follow one request across services: searches the configured trace fields (falls back to full text) on all streams and returns a chronological timeline, per-service steps with durations, and the first error.

trace_id.description: Correlation / request / trace id to follow
trace_id.title: Trace Id

range.description: Relative range ending now or at to_time: '15m', '2h', '1d'
range.title: Range

from_time.description: Absolute start, overrides range: ISO 8601 or 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM'
from_time.title: From Time

streams.description: Stream titles or ids; default the repository's focus, else all. ['*'] for everything
streams.title: Streams

instance.description: Instance from describe, e.g. 'payment/prod'; the default when omitted
instance.title: Instance

tools.name: compare_periods
tools.title: Compare periods
tools.description: Compare two periods (default: last window vs the one before; or around split_at). Lists groups that are new, increased, gone or decreased, normalised per hour. Defaults to errors only.

split_at.description: Point in time (e.g. a deploy); compares [split-window, split] with [split, split+window]
split_at.title: Split At

window.description: Length of each period when using split_at or the default
window.title: Window

current_to.description: Explicit current period end; default now
current_to.title: Current To

errors_only.description: AND the configured error query (default true)
errors_only.title: Errors Only

streams.description: Stream titles or ids; default the repository's focus, else all. ['*'] for everything
streams.title: Streams

instance.description: Instance from describe, e.g. 'payment/prod'; the default when omitted
instance.title: Instance

tools.name: scan
tools.title: Scan
tools.description: Health scan in one call: runs every scan rule (crashes, resource exhaustion, error spikes, new error types, 5xx, timeouts/connectivity, database, auth failures, plus the rules in the config) concurrently with exact counts against a baseline, and returns only what fired, most severe first, with the query, top groups and a sample. Start here for 'is anything wrong?', 'scan for errors', 'check X'. For a specific need pass rules (names/tags) or checks (ad hoc rules).

range.description: Window to scan, ending now (or at to_time): '15m', '1h', '24h'
range.title: Range

from_time.description: Absolute start, overrides range: ISO 8601 or 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM'
from_time.title: From Time

baseline.description: Length of the normal period right before the window, to compare rates with; same as the window by default. A longer one ('24h') is steadier for spiky traffic
baseline.title: Baseline

baseline_shift.description: Seasonal baseline instead: compare with the same window shifted back by this ('1d' for the same hour yesterday, '7d' for last week), several times; the median period is the reference. Use it for traffic with a daily or weekly curve
baseline_shift.title: Baseline Shift

baseline_periods.description: How many shifted periods baseline_shift compares with
baseline_periods.title: Baseline Periods

rules.description: Rule names or tags from describe(what='scan_rules') (e.g. ['errors'], ['database']); all rules when omitted, unless checks is given (then add 'all' to run them too)
rules.title: Rules

checks.description: Ad hoc rules for what the user asks to scan, same keys as a configured rule: {'name': 'declined', 'query': 'message:declined', 'threshold': 0} fires on any match; {'query': '...', 'growth': 2, 'min_count': 10} on a doubled rate; {'errors_only': true, 'group_by': 'exception', 'new_groups': true} on new error groups. Add 'per_traffic': true to a growth check on anything that follows traffic (errors, 5xx, timeouts) so it compares shares of traffic, with 'traffic_query' for what counts as traffic. Optional keys: severity, exclude, baseline, baseline_shift, confidence (default 0.99), group_by
checks.title: Checks

query.description: Extra Lucene filter applied to every rule, e.g. 'env:prod'
query.title: Query

streams.description: Stream titles or ids; default the repository's focus, else all. ['*'] for everything
streams.title: Streams

min_severity.description: Run only rules at least this severe: critical | high | medium | low
min_severity.title: Min Severity

samples.description: Attach one sample message per finding
samples.title: Samples

instance.description: Instance from describe, e.g. 'payment/prod'; the default when omitted
instance.title: Instance

tools.name: root_cause
tools.title: Root cause
tools.description: Find which service broke first and why. Compares every service's errors, traffic and latency with a baseline, pins the first error of each to the millisecond, detects deploys/restarts/host rollouts from the logs, infers the call graph from traces, and returns a ranked verdict with a timeline and evidence. Start here for 'what is causing this incident?'. view='changes': only the deploys and restarts found in the logs (new version-field values, host rollouts, start/stop lines). view='service_map': only which service calls which, from sampled traces, with traffic, error rate and p50/p95 latency per edge.

range.description: Window to analyse (the incident): '30m', '1h'; 6h for changes, else 1h
range.title: Range

from_time.description: Absolute start, overrides range: ISO 8601 or 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM'
from_time.title: From Time

baseline.description: verdict: length of the normal period right before the window; same as the window
baseline.title: Baseline

query.description: Optional Lucene filter for scope, e.g. 'env:prod'
query.title: Query

streams.description: Stream titles or ids; default the repository's focus, else all. ['*'] for everything
streams.title: Streams

sample.description: service_map: number of traces to sample (200)
sample.title: Sample

instance.description: Instance from describe, e.g. 'payment/prod'; the default when omitted
instance.title: Instance

tools.name: ask
tools.title: Ask
tools.description: Answer a plain-language question such as 'why did checkout fail on prod this morning?': finds the error the question describes, follows its trace across services, and states what it understood (environment, period) so it can be corrected. Asks back when the question is too vague. Sends TypeSafe the question and redacted, size-capped error text (250 characters each); never raw logs.

question.description: The question in the user's own words, in any language
question.title: Question

instance.description: Instance from describe, e.g. 'payment/prod'; the default when omitted
instance.title: Instance

tools.name: describe
tools.title: Describe
tools.description: What is there to query. 'instances': configured Graylog instances with detected version, the API in use and active redaction rules. 'streams': streams (id, title, description) the token can read. 'fields': field names (and types where available), plus the configured trace fields and error query; use before writing queries on unfamiliar logs. 'presets': named queries from the configuration. 'scan_rules': scan rules with their query, condition, severity and tags.

contains.description: fields: only names containing this text
contains.title: Contains

instance.description: Instance from describe, e.g. 'payment/prod'; the default when omitted
instance.title: Instance

tools.name: run_preset
tools.title: Run preset
tools.description: Run a named preset query, optionally overriding its arguments.

instance.description: Instance from describe, e.g. 'payment/prod'; the default when omitted
instance.title: Instance
